about.title: A surgeon who listens before he operates
paragraphs: Dr. Ahmed Shoulah is a consultant of general and laparoscopic surgery, holding a doctorate (MD) in general surgery and membership of the Royal College of Surgeons of England (MRCS).

He has performed thousands of procedures, from laparoscopic gallbladder removal and complex hernia repair to laser treatment of anorectal conditions and thyroid surgery, always guided by one principle: the right operation, for the right patient, at the right time.

items.question: How do I book an appointment?
items.answer: You can book through the contact form on this website, call the clinic directly or send us a message on WhatsApp. We will confirm your appointment and send you the clinic location.

items.question: What should I bring to my first consultation?
items.answer: Please bring any previous medical reports, recent lab results, ultrasound or CT scans, and a list of the medications you take regularly.

items.question: How long is recovery after laparoscopic surgery?
items.answer: Most patients walk on the same day, go home within 24 hours and return to light daily activities within one week. Recovery time varies with the procedure and your general health.

items.question: Will the surgery leave visible scars?
items.answer: Laparoscopic surgery uses incisions of 5–10 mm that usually fade to barely visible marks within months. Where possible, incisions are placed in natural skin creases.

hero.title: Dr. Ahmed Shoulah
hero.description: Consultant of general & laparoscopic surgery, combining academic excellence, international training and a deeply personal approach to patient care.

message.title: Surgery is a responsibility before it is a profession
paragraphs: When a patient walks into my clinic, they are trusting me with more than a diagnosis. They are trusting me with their health, their time and often their fears. I never take that trust lightly.

Over the years I have learned that the best surgical outcomes start long before the operating room: with careful listening, an honest explanation and a plan we build together. Sometimes the best advice is that you do not need surgery at all.
When surgery is the right choice, I am committed to performing it with the most precise, least invasive technique available, and to staying by your side until you have fully recovered.

categories.title: Laparoscopic & GI Surgery
categories.summary: Keyhole surgery for the gallbladder, appendix, stomach and intestines.
categories.description: Laparoscopic (keyhole) surgery uses a high-definition camera and fine instruments inserted through small incisions. Compared with open surgery, it means less pain, a shorter hospital stay, smaller scars and a faster return to normal life.

procedures.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
procedures.description: Removal of the gallbladder for symptomatic gallstones, cholecystitis or polyps. Usually a 45–60 minute procedure with discharge within 24 hours.

procedures.title: Laparoscopic appendectomy
procedures.description: Rapid, safe removal of an inflamed appendix through three small incisions, reducing wound infection and recovery time.

procedures.title: Anti-reflux surgery & hiatal hernia repair
procedures.description: Laparoscopic fundoplication to repair a hiatal hernia and control chronic reflux when medication is no longer enough.

procedures.title: Diagnostic laparoscopy
procedures.description: A minimally invasive look inside the abdomen to diagnose unexplained pain, with treatment in the same session when needed.

categories.title: Abdominal Wall & Hernia Surgery
categories.summary: Durable repair of all hernia types using modern mesh techniques.
categories.description: A hernia will not heal on its own and tends to enlarge over time. Modern repair, laparoscopic or open with lightweight mesh, offers durable results with low recurrence rates and a quick return to activity.

procedures.title: Inguinal hernia repair (TAPP / TEP)
procedures.description: Laparoscopic repair of groin hernias, including bilateral and recurrent cases, with less post-operative pain.

procedures.title: Umbilical & paraumbilical hernia repair
procedures.description: Repair of hernias around the navel with careful attention to the cosmetic result.

procedures.title: Incisional hernia repair
procedures.description: Repair of hernias that develop through previous surgical scars, using laparoscopic or open mesh techniques.

procedures.title: Diastasis recti & abdominal wall reconstruction
procedures.description: Restoring the strength and shape of the abdominal wall after pregnancy or previous surgery.

categories.title: Anorectal Surgery
categories.summary: Modern, low-pain treatment of hemorrhoids, fissures and fistulas.
categories.description: Anorectal conditions are common and highly treatable. Using laser and other modern techniques, most procedures are day cases with markedly less pain and a quicker return to work than traditional surgery.

procedures.title: Laser hemorrhoidoplasty
procedures.description: Shrinks hemorrhoids from within using laser energy: minimal pain, no open wounds and a fast recovery.

procedures.title: Anal fissure treatment
procedures.description: From medical therapy and botulinum toxin to lateral internal sphincterotomy for chronic fissures.

procedures.title: Anal fistula surgery
procedures.description: Sphincter-preserving techniques, including laser (FiLaC) and seton placement, to protect continence.

procedures.title: Pilonidal sinus treatment
procedures.description: Minimally invasive and flap techniques that reduce recurrence and shorten healing time.

categories.title: Endocrine Surgery
categories.summary: Thyroid, parathyroid and adrenal surgery with nerve-sparing precision.
categories.description: Endocrine surgery demands meticulous technique. Intra-operative nerve monitoring and careful preservation of the parathyroid glands help protect your voice and calcium balance.

procedures.title: Total thyroidectomy
procedures.description: Complete removal of the thyroid for multinodular goitre, Graves’ disease or confirmed cancer.

procedures.title: Hemithyroidectomy (lobectomy)
procedures.description: Removal of one thyroid lobe for a single suspicious or enlarging nodule, often preserving natural thyroid function.

procedures.title: Parathyroidectomy
procedures.description: Targeted removal of an overactive parathyroid gland to correct high calcium levels and protect bones and kidneys.

procedures.title: Laparoscopic adrenalectomy
procedures.description: Keyhole removal of adrenal tumours with less pain and a faster recovery than open surgery.

faq.title: Everything you want to know about your surgery

items.question: Is laparoscopic surgery safer than open surgery?
items.answer: For most suitable patients, laparoscopic surgery carries a lower risk of wound infection and incisional hernia, causes less pain and allows a faster recovery. The best approach for you depends on your condition and medical history, which we assess at consultation.

items.question: How long will I stay in hospital?
items.answer: Many procedures, such as laser hemorrhoid treatment and most hernia repairs, are day cases. Laparoscopic gallbladder removal usually needs one night, while thyroid surgery typically requires one to two nights.

items.question: When can I return to work?
items.answer: Office work is usually possible within 5–10 days after most laparoscopic procedures. Jobs that involve heavy lifting may require 3–4 weeks. You will receive a personalised plan before discharge.

items.question: Can a hernia heal without surgery?
items.answer: No. A hernia is a defect in the abdominal wall and does not close on its own. Support belts may ease symptoms but do not treat the cause, and delaying repair raises the risk of complications such as strangulation.

items.question: Is laser hemorrhoid treatment painful?
items.answer: Laser treatment causes significantly less pain than traditional surgery because there are no open wounds. Most patients need only simple pain relief and return to daily activities within a few days.

items.question: Can thyroid surgery affect my voice?
items.answer: Temporary hoarseness can occur, but permanent voice change is rare in experienced hands. We use intra-operative nerve monitoring and meticulous technique to protect the laryngeal nerves.

items.question: What tests will I need before surgery?
items.answer: Typically blood tests, an ECG and imaging relevant to your condition. Depending on your age and health, an anaesthesia assessment or specialist review may also be requested.

items.question: Can I send my reports before booking?
items.answer: Yes. You can send your reports and scans via WhatsApp for an initial review, and we will advise you on the most appropriate next step.

items.title: Laparoscopic Gallbladder Removal: A Complete Patient Guide
items.excerpt: Everything you need to know about gallstones, when surgery is recommended, what happens on the day and how quickly you can expect to recover.
items.intro: Gallstones are one of the most common digestive problems. Many people never develop symptoms, but when stones cause pain, inflammation or complications, removing the gallbladder laparoscopically is the definitive and safest treatment.

sections.heading: When is surgery recommended?
paragraphs: Surgery is usually advised if you have recurrent episodes of upper-right abdominal pain (biliary colic), an inflamed gallbladder (cholecystitis), gallstone pancreatitis or stones that have passed into the bile duct. Silent stones discovered incidentally often only need monitoring.

sections.heading: What happens during the operation?
paragraphs: Under general anaesthesia, four small incisions of 5–10 mm are made. A high-definition camera guides the surgeon to separate and remove the gallbladder safely. The operation typically takes 45–60 minutes.

sections.heading: Recovery and life without a gallbladder
paragraphs: Most patients walk within hours, go home within 24 hours and return to office work within a week.
The liver continues to produce bile, so digestion adapts quickly. Some people simply find that very fatty meals are best enjoyed in moderation during the first few weeks.

items.title: Inguinal Hernia: Symptoms, Risks and When to Have Surgery
items.excerpt: A bulge in the groin is more than a cosmetic issue. Learn how hernias develop, which symptoms need urgent care and why early repair is often wiser.
items.intro: An inguinal hernia occurs when part of the intestine or fatty tissue pushes through a weak spot in the lower abdominal wall, creating a bulge in the groin. It is far more common in men and can appear at any age.

sections.heading: Common symptoms
paragraphs: A swelling that increases with coughing, straining or standing and disappears when lying down, together with a dragging or aching sensation in the groin, especially by the end of the day.

sections.heading: When is it an emergency?
paragraphs: Seek urgent care if the bulge becomes firm and painful and cannot be pushed back, or if it is accompanied by vomiting or an inability to pass gas. These may be signs of a strangulated hernia, which requires immediate surgery.

sections.heading: Why choose laparoscopic repair?
paragraphs: Laparoscopic repair (TAPP or TEP) places a mesh behind the abdominal wall through small incisions. It allows both sides to be repaired in one session and is associated with less pain and a faster return to activity.

items.title: Hemorrhoids: Modern Treatment Options Beyond Traditional Surgery
items.excerpt: Hemorrhoids are common and very treatable. Discover the options available today, from lifestyle changes to low-pain laser procedures.
items.intro: Hemorrhoids are swollen blood vessels in the anal canal that can cause bleeding, itching, discomfort or prolapse. Embarrassment often delays treatment, yet most cases can be managed simply and effectively.

sections.heading: Start with the basics
paragraphs: Increasing dietary fibre, drinking enough water and avoiding prolonged straining or sitting on the toilet resolve many early cases. Topical treatments can relieve symptoms during flare-ups.

sections.heading: Clinic procedures
paragraphs: For persistent internal hemorrhoids, rubber band ligation is a quick clinic procedure that cuts off the blood supply to the hemorrhoid so that it shrinks and falls off within days.

sections.heading: Laser hemorrhoidoplasty
paragraphs: Advanced or recurrent hemorrhoids can be treated with laser energy delivered from within. There are no open wounds, pain is minimal and most patients return to work within a few days.

items.title: Thyroid Nodules: Understanding Your Diagnosis
items.excerpt: Most thyroid nodules are benign. Here is how doctors evaluate them and the specific situations in which surgery becomes the right choice.
items.intro: Thyroid nodules are lumps within the thyroid gland. They are extremely common, often found on a routine ultrasound, and more than 90% are benign. The key is a careful, structured evaluation.

sections.heading: How nodules are evaluated
paragraphs: Assessment combines thyroid function tests, a high-resolution ultrasound that grades the nodule’s features and, when indicated, a fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy.

sections.heading: When is surgery recommended?
paragraphs: Surgery is considered for nodules that are suspicious or malignant on biopsy, large nodules causing pressure symptoms such as difficulty swallowing or breathing, overactive (toxic) nodules, or for cosmetic concerns.

sections.heading: What surgery involves
paragraphs: Depending on the findings, one lobe (hemithyroidectomy) or the entire gland (total thyroidectomy) is removed through a small incision placed in a natural skin crease of the neck, with nerve monitoring to protect the voice.

items.title: Preparing for Surgery: A Practical Checklist
items.excerpt: Good preparation means a smoother operation and a faster recovery. Use this checklist in the days and hours before your procedure.
items.intro: Feeling prepared reduces anxiety and helps your body recover. These practical steps apply to most planned general surgery procedures; your surgical team will give you instructions specific to your case.

sections.heading: One to two weeks before
paragraphs: Complete the requested blood tests and scans, review your regular medications with the doctor (especially blood thinners and diabetes medication) and stop smoking to lower the risk of complications.

sections.heading: The day before
paragraphs: Prepare loose, comfortable clothing, arrange for someone to accompany you home and follow the fasting instructions carefully, usually no food for six hours before surgery.

sections.heading: On the day of surgery
paragraphs: Shower, remove jewellery and nail polish, bring your reports and ID, and tell the team about any new symptoms such as a fever or a cough.

items.title: Appendicitis: Warning Signs You Shouldn’t Ignore
items.excerpt: Appendicitis can progress quickly. Recognising the early symptoms and seeking help promptly can prevent serious complications.
items.intro: Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix and one of the most common surgical emergencies. It can affect anyone, but it is most frequent between the ages of 10 and 30.

sections.heading: Classic symptoms
paragraphs: Pain that starts around the navel and moves to the lower right abdomen over several hours, loss of appetite, nausea or vomiting, and a low-grade fever. The pain often worsens with walking or coughing.

sections.heading: Why timing matters
paragraphs: If treatment is delayed, the inflamed appendix can perforate and cause peritonitis or an abscess, leading to a longer hospital stay. Avoid painkillers and laxatives until you have been assessed, as they may mask symptoms.

sections.heading: Treatment
paragraphs: Laparoscopic appendectomy is the standard treatment. Most patients go home within 24–48 hours and return to normal activities within one to two weeks.

items.title: Recovery After Abdominal Surgery: Nutrition and Activity Tips
items.excerpt: What you eat and how you move after surgery directly affect healing. Follow these practical tips for a smoother, faster recovery.
items.intro: Recovery does not end when you leave the hospital. The choices you make in the following weeks, such as what you eat, how you move and how you care for your wounds, make a real difference to how quickly you heal.

sections.heading: Eat to heal
paragraphs: Start with light meals and increase gradually. Prioritise protein (eggs, fish, chicken, legumes), fruit and vegetables for vitamins, and plenty of fluids. Fibre helps prevent constipation, especially while you are taking pain medication.

sections.heading: Move early, but wisely
paragraphs: Short, frequent walks from the first day improve circulation and reduce the risk of clots and chest infections. Avoid lifting anything heavier than 5 kg for about four weeks, or as advised.

sections.heading: When to call your surgeon
paragraphs: Contact us if you develop a fever, increasing redness or discharge from a wound, worsening abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or shortness of breath.
